articles.title: All Haunting Elegance Star Path Duties and Routine Duties - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Disney Dreamlight Valley's Haunting Elegance Star Path launches on September 23, 2026 as part of the Season of Scares update alongside new character Oogie
articles.body:
Disney Dreamlight Valley's Haunting Elegance Star Path launches on September 23, 2026 as part of the Season of Scares update alongside new character Oogie Boogie . Running throughout the month of October, this Star Path celebrates all things Halloween with new spooky outfits, furniture, accessories, and even a skeletal Dream Style for Scrooge McDuck!

Haunting Elegance Star Path Duties include tasks that celebrate the spooky season such as harvesting and cooking with Pumpkins , feeding Black Critters , and spending time with Jack Skellington and Sally . Completing these Duties will reward you with Tokens that you can spend on a variety of haunting rewards - and perhaps a few festive ones too, thanks to Sandy Claws!

Routine Duties also return for this Star Path. Three new Routine Duties are available each week on Wednesdays at 9:00 AM EST / 6:00 AM PST . Completing these earns you even more Tokens, which you can spend on Rewards and Bonus Rewards.

All Haunting Elegance Star Path Routine Duties

Three new Routine Duties for the Haunting Elegance Star Path unlock every Wednesday at 9:00 AM EST / 6:00 AM PST . You do not have to complete all three Routine Duties that week - uncompleted Duties will remain active for the remainder of the Star Path.

Players with the free version of the Star Path must complete each page of Routine Duties before moving on to the next. However, players who have purchased the Premium Star Path using Moonstones can complete Routine Duties in any order.

articles.title: A Halloween Invasion Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: A Halloween Invasion is the first of several Quests required to unlock Oogie Boogiein Disney Dreamlight Valley. It first released on September 23, 2026. In
articles.body:
A Halloween Invasion is the first of several Quests required to unlock Oogie Boogie in Disney Dreamlight Valley . It first released on September 23, 2026. In this Quest, you help Scrooge McDuck investigate something strange in his Shop and end up meeting The Nightmare Before Christmas's iconic trickster in his lair!

Unlike other Villagers, Oogie Boogie is unlocked via a series of Quests released weekly. To unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in 2026, you MUST start "A Halloween Invasion" by November 11, 2026.

Once you have begun this Quest, you can complete the other Quests in the chain at your own pace - they will stick around after November 11.

If you missed Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return in October 2027!

Check your Mailbox to find a letter from Scrooge McDuck. Scrooge tells you that something strange has appeared in his Store, and asks for your help investigating it!

Head inside Scrooge's Store and talk to Scrooge. He tells you that he found a strange mirror in his Vault that he doesn't remember ever owning. When he put the mirror on display, it started glowing green!

The Strange Mirror is located to the left of Scrooge's desk, on the first floor of his store. Approach it and select "Interact." You read the words "Oogie Boogie" backwards on the mirror, and the mirror breaks! The "Interact" prompt turns into "Enter." Select "Enter" to find yourself in Oogie Boogie's Lair!

Talk to Oogie Boogie. He tells you that you, Merlin, and Scrooge trapped him in the mirror years ago because you were too scared of him. However, by breaking the mirror, you freed him, and now he wants to do business with you!

First, Oogie Boogie gives you three clothing items: a Lock Mask, a Shock Mask, and a Barrel Mask. He tells you that more fabulous prizes await if you spin his Lucky Wheel!

The Lucky Wheel is located in the top left corner of Oogie Boogie's Lair, not far from where the creature himself is standing. Walk up to it and select "Interact." However, nothing happens - as the wheel is broken!

Talk to Oogie Boogie. He tells you that he needs something called "Fear Essence" to repair the Lucky Wheel, and that you are going to help him harvest it by playing the mini-game Whack-A-Pumpkin !

Follow Oogie Boogie to the small open dirt area surrounded by a fence, located to the right of the Lucky Wheel. In this arena, you can play Whack-A-Pumpkin as many times as you like.

Press the pumpkin-shaped button on the stack of dice at the edge of the arena by approaching it and selecting "Interact."

Pumpkins will appear randomly on the 3 x 3 dirt grid inside the arena. Whack Pumpkins using your Royal Pickaxe.

For each Pumpkin you whack, you will generally receive between 1 and 3 Fear Essence. Make sure to pick up the Fear Essence as it drops!

There is a pumpkin-shaped timer on the wall that shows you how much time you have left in your current game of Whack-a-Pumpkin. However, don't worry - you can play as many rounds as you like, just keep pressing the button again and again!

You must whack a total of 10 Pumpkins and collect a total of 10 Fear Essence. When you have completed this goal, bring the Fear Essence to Oogie Boogie.

Here are some handy tips to help you whack as many pumpkins as possible in each round!

Equip your Royal Pickaxe before starting the game

Because Pumpkins pop up so quickly, and you can play as many times as you like, you shouldn't attempt to cover every spot. Instead, stand in a corner of the arena where you can reach 3-5 spots and focus on whacking ONLY the pumpkins that appear near you!

Even if a Pumpkin is starting to descend back into the ground, still hit it with your Pickaxe - you might still get some Fear Essence!

Unequip any Companions before playing Whack-a-Pumpkin. They have a tendency to wander around the arena and block your path.

Once you've given the Fear Essence to Oogie Boogie, Interact with the Lucky Wheel again. This time, the wheel spins - but you don't get a prize!

Talk to Oogie Boogie. He tells you that you were unlucky, and landed on "Halloween Curse." Bugs and pumpkins have appeared all around the Valley, and it's up to you to clean them up!

Leave Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Mirror and return to the Valley. You will need to clean up Oogie Boogie Bugs from Mickey Mouse's House and Goofy's House and clean up Sweet or Spooky Pumpkins around the Valley! Some of the items will drop Fear Essence when you remove them, so make sure to pick up any Fear Essence you find.

Remove Oogie Boogie Bugs From Mickey's House

Head into Mickey Mouse's House. There are three swarms of Oogie Boogie Bugs inside. You can remove them by approaching them and selecting "Remove." The bugs can be found:

In the corner between the House door and Mickey's wardrobe

Remove Oogie Boogie Bugs From Goofy's House

Your next stop is Goofy's House. This time, there are four swarms of Oogie Boogie Bugs you need to remove. You can find them:

To the right of the large wooden dining table

Next, you will need to use your Royal Pickaxe to remove eight Sweet or Spooky Pumpkins around the Plaza and the Peaceful Meadow. These Pumpkins have a random effect - you might get a treat (several Fear Essence) or you might receive a trick (some spooky ghosts briefly appear)!

The Sweet or Spooky Pumpkins can be found in the following locations:

The first Sweet or Spooky Pumpkin is located in the top left corner of the Plaza, in front of the default location for the Player's House.

The second Sweet or Spooky Pumpkin can be found at the top of the stairs leading from the Plaza to the Peaceful Meadow.

Two more Sweet and Spooky Pumpkins are located in the bottom right corner of the Plaza, near the ramp leading down to the Peaceful Meadow. They are on the side of the Plaza near the Forest of Valor.

The fifth Sweet and Spooky Pumpkin is in the Peaceful Meadow. It is in the bottom right corner of the biome, hidden among some rocks.

You can find another Sweet and Spooky Pumpkin to the left of the southern-most pond in the Peaceful Meadow, just to the right of the default location of WALL-E's Garden.

There is also a Sweet and Spooky Pumpkin to the left of the upper of the small ponds in the Peaceful Meadow, pretty much directly north from where you found the last one!

Finally, you can find one more Sweet and Spooky Pumpkin in the top left corner of the Peaceful Meadow, right in front of a Rock Spot.

Once you have removed all Sweet and Spooky Pumpkins, you will have collected a total of 20 Fear Essence. Return to Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Strange Mirror in Scrooge's Store.

Head back to Oogie Boogie's Lair and give him the Fear Essence you collected. He tells you that he has something in mind to use it for, but it will take him a while to get ready. However, he does tell you to spin the Lucky Wheel one more time, promising you will get a real prize this time.

Interact with the Lucky Wheel again. This time, a Red Chest pops up - open it to find a Furniture Pouch containing the Oogie Boogie's Lair Skeletons decoration item!

The Quest concludes here. If you began this Quest before September 30, 2026, you must wait until that date to begin the next one - The Oogie Boogie Contract .

Up Next: The Oogie Boogie Contract Walkthrough

articles.title: The Oogie Boogie Contract Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Oogie Boogie Contract is the second in a series of Quests required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley. It initially released
articles.body:
The Oogie Boogie Contract is the second in a series of Quests required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley. It initially released on September 30, 2026.

This Quest begins a short while after completing Oogie Boogie's first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , during which you discovered the trickster trapped in his Lair inside a haunted mirror in Scrooge McDuck's Shop. However, it seems that Oogie Boogie's power is growing, because he's now able to reach beyond his Lair to send you a letter!

This guide explains everything you need to know about completing Oogie Boogie's Contract Quest, including where to find all Ghosties , how to equip the Ghost Lantern , and the exact ingredients you need to make the Snake and Spider Stew .

To unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you need to start his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , by November 11, 2026. Once you have started the first Quest, you can complete The Oogie Boogie Contract and all following Quests at your own pace without a time limit.

If you missed Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027.

Check your Mailbox to find a letter from Oogie Boogie. He offers you another chance to spin his Lucky Wheel, and attaches a Lucky Wheel Ticket to the letter.

With the Lucky Wheel in your inventory, head through the Strange Mirror in Scrooge's Store and enter Oogie Boogie's Lair. Give the Lucky Wheel Ticket to Oogie Boogie - he will be standing in the back corner of his Lair next to the Lucky Wheel!

Spin the Lucky Wheel by approaching the crank and selecting "Interact." It's not immediately obvious what happened, so talk to Oogie Boogie again. Oh, no - it seems you've landed on "Become Oogie Boogie's Minion!"

Oogie Boogie tells you that you now have a contract with him. If you do not serve as his minion, he will become powerful enough to leave his lair! There's nothing to do but fulfill his wishes, and the first thing he wants is for you to dress up like his minion and catch Ghosties in his lair.

The Boogeyman gives you a Ghost Lantern accessory and five U-Carve-It Pumpkin furniture items. Using the Wardrobe Menu , equip the following:

Lock Mask OR Shock Mask OR Barrel Mask (You obtained these masks during A Halloween Invasion )

Note that you need to equip the Ghost Lantern, not just put it on. You can do this by selecting the hand icon on the Tool Wheel and then pressing the indicated button ( Cross on any controller, Right Mouse Button on PC, R2 on Steam Deck).

With the Ghost Lantern equipped, run through the three Ghosties in Oogie Boogie's Lair. This will trap the Ghosties inside your Lantern. You can find the Ghosties in the following locations:

At the top of the right side set of stairs, on the opposite side of the Lair from where Oogie Boogie is standing

At the bottom of the right side set of stairs

At the bottom of the left side set of stairs, tucked in the corner between the staircase and the wall

Go back through the Strange Mirror and return to the Valley. Now, you have two options for how to progress through this Quest. Both options are equally valid, so choose whichever you like! You only have to do ONE of the two.

Decorate your Valley using five pieces of Halloween-themed furniture. You can find furniture that counts by selecting the "Halloween" tag under the "Style" sub-heading in the Furniture search menu.

The U-Carve-It Pumpkins Oogie Boogie gave you DO count as Halloween furniture! You can customize them using the Touch of Magic feature to design your own jack o' lanterns!

Decorate your Valley using five pieces of Cute furniture. You can find furniture that counts by selecting the "Cute" tag under the "Style" sub-heading in the Furniture search menu.

Now, it's time to fulfill Oogie Boogie's wishes and find some new players for his games!

Head to Mickey Mouse's House and talk to Mickey there. You can choose to warn Mickey about the Ghostie or release it without telling him - don't worry, either one will progress the Quest! The Ghosties will fill Mickey's House, and will either be frightened or calm depending on whether or not you warned him.

Next, go to the Dreamlight Library - aka Merlin's House - and talk to Merlin . Once again, you can tell him or surprise him, but the Ghosties will wind up released in his House either way.

Finally, head to Chez Remy and talk to Remy . Either warn him or release the Ghosties with no warning, with both options progressing the Quest.

However, things go a little bit differently this time. Only one Ghostie gets released, and he starts making trouble in the restaurant! This time, instead of equipping your Ghost Lantern and running through the Ghostie, you need to approach the Ghostie and select "Pick up."

The Ghostie will quickly move in a circle around the seating area of Chez Remy, before darting into the kitchen. The kitchen is the best place to catch it, because you can trap it in the small space by blocking the kitchen exit with your body. You can also sprint or glide to catch up to the fast-moving Ghostie.

After the Ghostie is caught, talk to Remy again to reassure him that everything is okay.

Return to Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Strange Mirror in Scrooge's Store. Talk to Oogie Boogie, who will either be satisfied with your work (if you scared the villagers) or disappointed (if you warned them). Regardless of your choice, however, he decides to keep you as his minion and assigns you another task: cook Snake and Spider Stew to entertain Oogie Boogie's guests.

Follow Oogie Boogie to the Cooking Station (shaped like a giant cauldron) in the bottom right corner of his lair. Next to the Cooking Station is a rack of ingredients containing everything you'll need to make Snake and Spider Stew. Read the paper pinned to the wall to receive the following clue:

Here are some more hints about what you need to choose from the ingredient rack for your Snake and Spider Stew:

The hint outright tells you that you need Eggs

For the second ingredient, look for something described as Mushy

For the third ingredient, look for something long and skinny like a snake

The three ingredients you will need to make the Snake and Spider Stew are Tap to Reveal . Grab one of each of the three ingredients you need and add them to the Cauldron to make Snake and Spider Stew.

Bring the Snake and Spider Stew to Oogie Boogie . He decides that you have done well enough as his minion, and releases you from your contract. He even gives you a reward - a Ghost Well furniture item!

The Quest concludes here, with Oogie Boogie telling you to leave his lair but inviting you to come back soon as he has more tasks that he's going to require your help with.

If you began this Quest before October 7, 2026, you must wait until that date to begin the next one. If the next Quest has unlocked, you just need to wait for your next letter from Oogie Boogie !

Up Next: The Ghost in the Portrait Walkthrough

articles.title: Oogie Boogie - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Oogie Boogie is a trickster who lives in Halloween Town in Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas. He loves playing games and making deals - but only
articles.body:
Oogie Boogie is a trickster who lives in Halloween Town in Tim Burton's The Nightmare Before Christmas. He loves playing games and making deals - but only if the games are rigged in his favor! In Disney Dreamlight Valley's Season of Scares update , you learn that Oogie Boogie was trapped inside a mirror dimension long ago. But he's not content to stay trapped anymore - the Boogieman wants to free himself and cause chaos in the Valley!

This character guide will tell you everything you need to know about Oogie Boogie, including his unique unlock process , which involves completing a series of Quests initially released weekly, and all the spooky rewards you can earn by freeing and befriending him!

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 11, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 11.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

Looking for something in particular? Click the links below to to jump directly to...

Unlocking Oogie Boogie as a Villager is a bit of a tricky process. You must complete a series of six Quests, which were initially released weekly throughout September and October 2026. You must start the first Quest by November 4, 2026. If you do not do this, Oogie Boogie will leave the Valley until October 2027. If you missed Oogie Boogie in 2026, you can unlock him when the Halloween season rolls around again!

A Halloween Invasion - unlocks September 23, 2026. Open the path to Oogie Boogie's lair, then clean up the Halloween chaos he spreads around the Valley!

The Oogie Boogie Contract - unlocks September 30, 2026. An unlucky wheel spin sees you serving Oogie Boogie as his minion and finding new players for his rigged games!

The Ghost in the Portrait - unlocks October 7, 2026. Free Jack Skellington's dog Zero from the Haunted Portrait Oogie Boogie has trapped him in by collecting Essence and making some Ghostly Paint Thinner!

Rescue Mission - unlocks October 14, 2026. Find the fake furniture in Oogie Boogie's Lair, then craft Extra-Strength Bug Spray to keep your friends safe from his tricks!

Let the Games Begin - unlocks October 21, 2026. Play four mini-games to collect Oogie Boogie Tiles, then solve a tile puzzle featuring Oogie Boogie's terrifying face!

Oogie Boogie's Big Game - unlocks October 28, 2026. Win Oogie Boogie's quiz game to officially bring him to the Valley as a Villager!

Oogie Boogie's Quests center around spinning his Lucky Wheel and dealing with the chaos that results, as well as playing various mini-games available in his Lair. Most of the Quests in this chain will begin with receiving a letter in your Mailbox and needing to travel through the mirror in Scrooge's Store to meet Oogie Boogie in the dimension where he has been trapped.

Oogie Boogie's favorite Gifts are spooky items that remind him of Halloween. Some of his favorite items include:

All Oogie Boogie Friendship Rewards & Quest Rewards

In addition to Friendship Rewards earned by having Daily Discussions with, Hanging Out with, and giving Gifts to Oogie Boogie, this scheming trickster is surprisingly generous with his Quest rewards. Most of Oogie Boogie's unlock Quests include at least one reward to help make your Valley just a little bit spookier!

Up Next: Friendship Guide: Assigning Roles

articles.title: The Ghost in the Portrait Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: The Ghost in the Portrait is the third Quest in the Quest chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley. It was initially
articles.body:
The Ghost in the Portrait is the third Quest in the Quest chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager in Disney Dreamlight Valley . It was initially released on October 7, 2026. To begin this Quest, you must have completed the previous two Oogie Boogie Quests , A Halloween Invasion and The Oogie Boogie Contract .

Once you have fulfilled the requirements, you will receive a letter from Oogie Boogie in your Mailbox. Oogie Boogie will say that he noticed you were interested in his Haunted Portrait, invite you to return to his Lair, and give you another Lucky Wheel Ticket.

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 11, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 11.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

With the Lucky Wheel Ticket in your Inventory, enter Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Strange Mirror in Scrooge's Store. Head up the stairs to where Oogie Boogie is waiting next to his Lucky Wheel.

However, rather than talking to Oogie Boogie, you need to investigate the Haunted Portrait by walking up to it and selecting "Interact." You realize that Zero, Jack Skellington's beloved ghostly dog companion, is trapped inside!

A Memory Puzzle appears, titled "A Skeleton and His Ghost Dog ." Interact with it to solve the puzzle. Memory Puzzles are jigsaw-type puzzles first introduced as Tapestry Puzzles in the Storybook Vale expansion . You need to rotate the pieces and put them in the correct places to complete a picture puzzle.

Here are some hints to help you solve this Memory Puzzle:

The pieces shaped like Zero and Oogie Boogie are extremely distinctive in shape, so try placing them first!

The completed picture shows Zero on the left and Jack Skellington on the right.

The image is mostly black in color, but there are gray and white trees to the left of Zero and to the right of Jack.

The completed Memory Puzzle looks like this:

The Ghost in the Portrait - Solved Memory Puzzle

Talk to Oogie Boogie. He admits that Zero is trapped in the portrait, and that the only way to save him is to win Ghostly Paint Thinner as a prize from the Lucky Wheel. However, you know from your previous spins that Oogie Boogie has rigged the wheel, so you decide to get a little help first!

Talk to Scrooge McDuck. He will either be inside his Store or wandering around Oogie Boogie's Lair. Merlin will show up too, and the pair will suggest that you distract Oogie Boogie and then use your Royal Pickaxe to fix the rigged wheel.

They will give you a Plain Gift Box that has been rigged to explode. Head to the bottom of the right-side staircase in Oogie Boogie's Lair. This is the staircase on the opposite side of the room from Oogie Boogie and his Lucky Wheel. There is a sparkling spot next to a stack of jack o'lanterns. Interact with the sparkling spot to place the Plain Gift there.

As soon as you have placed the Plain Gift Box, Oogie Boogie will run down the stairs to check it out. Head back to the Lucky Wheel and hit it once with your Royal Pickaxe. The following items will fall out, so pick up them all:

From your Inventory, Use the Ghostly Paint Thinner to upgrade your Royal Watering Can. Then, water the Haunted Portrait with your Royal Watering Can.

The portrait dissolves into ghosts, but Zero does not appear. Oogie Boogie tricked you yet again! Talk to Oogie Boogie, who is furious. He causes the Mirror Lair to be filled with a large number of Haunted Portraits, and challenges you to find and water the correct one.

The correct Haunted Portrait is the only one in which Zero appears. The fake portraits all show an empty scene, with no ghost dog. The correct painting is Tap to Reveal

Water the correct portrait with your Haunted Watering Can. Unfortunately, it doesn't work, and Zero remains stuck!

Talk to Merlin, who will likely be hanging out in Oogie Boogie's Lair. If he isn't there, however, you can generally find him in or near his House . Merlin tells you that Zero is frightened, and is sending his essence out of the portrait and into the world. Collecting the Zero Essence will let you craft it into something magical to free him!

There are five Zero drawings hidden around Oogie Boogie's Lair. You will need to find them all, approach each one, and select "Remove" to collect the glowing white Zero Essence that spawns.

The five Zero Drawings are found in the following locations:

The first drawing is in the window display area at the base of the right-side staircase, not far from where you placed the Plain Gift Box.

After claiming the first Zero Essence, turn around. The second drawing is on top of the table at the base of the right staircase, near the Plain Gift Box.

Go around to the other side of the right staircase, to where there is a small alcove filled with cobwebs. In this narrow space, turn around and look at the side of the staircase. The third Zero Drawing is on the side of the staircase, about halfway up.

The fourth drawing is on the back of a stack of dice to the left of the glowing lava pool, near the real Haunted Portrait.

After claiming the fourth Zero Essence, turn around. Immediately behind you, on the wall behind the warped version of Scrooge's desk, is the final drawing, hidden among some Oogie Boogie's Lair Skeletons.

Once you have collected all five Zero Essence orbs, head to the Crafting Station next to the mirror leading back to Dreamlight Valley. At the Crafting Station, combine the five Zero Essence into the Real Ghostly Paint Thinner.

From your Inventory, Use the Real Ghostly Paint Thinner to add it to your Royal Watering Can. Then, use your Royal Watering Can to water the genuine Haunted Portrait - the one at the base of the left-side staircase.

This time, Zero is freed from the portrait! He will join you as a Notable Companion . Equip Zero as your Companion and level him up to earn lots of exciting rewards, including an exclusive Zero's Bed Furniture item.

Talk to Oogie Boogie to complete the Quest. He tells you to leave his lair, as he is furious and has plans to cook up to get back at you for getting the upper hand today!

articles.title: Rescue Mission Walkthrough - Disney Dreamlight Valley Guide - IGN
articles.summary: Rescue Mission is the fourth Quest in the Disney Dreamlight Valley Quest chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager. It initially released on October
articles.body:
Rescue Mission is the fourth Quest in the Disney Dreamlight Valley Quest chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager. It initially released on October 14, 2026. To begin this Quest, you must have completed the previous three: A Halloween Invasion , The Oogie Boogie Contract , and The Ghost in the Portrait .

At the end of The Ghost in the Portrait, you will unlock Zero, Jack Skellington's ghostly dog, as a Companion . Oogie Boogie is furious with you for freeing his captive, and he has some sneaky plans up his burlap sleeve!

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 11, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 11.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

Some time after completing The Ghost in the Portrait, you will receive a threatening letter from Oogie Boogie in your Mailbox. Read the letter, then head through the mirror in Scrooge's Store and enter Oogie Boogie's Lair to officially start the Quest.

You will find Oogie Boogie threatening Merlin for his involvement in helping you. He reminds Merlin that, when you worked as his minion during The Oogie Boogie Contract, you made it so that he can trap Merlin, Goofy, and Mickey Mouse in his Lair whenever he wants.

Talk to Oogie Boogie, who is not willing to listen to you. Instead, he makes you play another game: finding the artificial furniture in his Lair.

To beat Oogie Boogie's latest challenge, you must locate and interact with five fake pieces of Furniture and Decor scattered around his Lair. You can identify the fake items because they are glowing green.

Walk up to each Furniture piece and select "Interact." This will cause the fake item to disappear. The pieces you need to interact with are:

The display stand located at the bottom of the right staircase, next to the large window.

The potion bottles on top of the mirror version of Scrooge's Desk.

The lamp attached to the pillar between Scrooge's desk and the item display shelves, on the left side near the Wall Skeletons.

The bear-shaped pillow on the couch at the bottom of the left staircase.

The hanging planter on the wall in the narrow alcove to the left of the left staircase, just past the couch where the fake pillow was.

Talk to Oogie Boogie. He refuses to release the Villagers he has trapped in his lair, and simply laughs at you.

Talk to Merlin, who will still be in Oogie Boogie's Lair. Scrooge McDuck will show up as well. They will realize that Oogie Boogie is getting stronger because of all the Fear Essence in the Valley, and that you need to find his weakness before you can come up with a plan. You realize that Zero will be able to sniff it out for you!

Equip Zero as your Companion using the Wardrobe Menu. Then, with Zero equipped, talk to Oogie Boogie again. As you are simply distracting him while Zero sniffs out his weakness, you can choose any dialogue options here - it will not change the outcome.

Zero dropped the items he found at the bottom of the left staircase. Pick up the book on the ground and look at it in your Inventory to find a recipe for Extra-Strength Bug Spray . Oogie Boogie is powered by bugs, so this will definitely affect him!

Make Extra-Strength Bug Spray using the recipe provided in Oogie Boogie's Diary:

Lava Core x 1 - Fished from the lava pit in the center of the downstairs area of Oogie Boogie's Lair

Skeleton Fish x 1 - Fished from the lava pit in the center of the downstairs area of Oogie Boogie's Lair

"A Fragrant, Perfectly Tended Flower" - Talk to Goofy, who will be hanging out in the Lair, and he will give you a Dandelion

Dream Shards x 10 - found by digging up sparkling spots in any Biome, dropped when removing Night Thorns, Splinters of Fate, or Inkies, dropped when feeding any Critter its favorite food. (If you do not have ten Dream Shards, you may need to leave Oogie Boogie's Lair to collect them.)

Give one bottle of Extra-Strength Bug Spray to Merlin and one to Scrooge McDuck. They should both still be in Oogie Boogie's Lair.

Once both characters have their bug spray, talk to Oogie Boogie. Merlin and Scrooge will appear, and the three of you will confront him together. Oogie Boogie realizes that he cannot harm Merlin or Scrooge now that they have the Bug Spray, but he will tell you that he is not done yet, and will come up with even more evil plans in the future.

Although he is mad at you, Oogie Boogie still gives you a reward: an Oogie Boogie Decorative Bats furniture item to make your Valley look more like Halloween Town! The Quest ends here, and you will need to wait until Oogie Boogie sends you another letter to begin the next one.

articles.summary: After you derailed Oogie Boogie's plans in The Ghost in the Portrait and Rescue Mission, Halloween Town's resident trickster has cooked up his
articles.body:
After you derailed Oogie Boogie's plans in The Ghost in the Portrait and Rescue Mission , Halloween Town's resident trickster has cooked up his biggest scheme yet. In Let the Games Begin, the fifth Quest in the chain required to unlock Oogie Boogie as a Villager , you will have to return to the Boogieman's lair and survive a gauntlet of devilishly tricky games!

Let the Games Begin initially released on October 21, 2026. You must have completed Oogie Boogie's previous Quests , up through Rescue Mission , to begin it. Like the previous Quests in the series, it will begin when you receive a letter from Oogie Boogie in your Mailbox.

Important PSA for Unlocking Oogie Boogie

If you want to unlock Oogie Boogie in 2026, you MUST begin his first Quest, A Halloween Invasion , no later than November 11, 2026. Once you have begun the first Quest, the other five can be completed at any time once they have unlocked.

As long as you have STARTED A Halloween Invasion, you will be able to unlock Oogie Boogie, even if you finish up the Quest chain after November 11.

If you missed out on Oogie Boogie in 2026, he will return to the Valley in October 2027 !

Oogie Boogie's letter will blame you for breaking his Lucky Wheel in the previous Quests and demand that you make him a new one. He will send you a Lucky Wheel Cog, which you must use alongside the five Lucky Wheel Cogs you previously picked up when breaking the Wheel during the Quest The Ghost in the Portrait .

At any Crafting Station in the Valley, use the six Lucky Wheel Cogs to craft a Genuinely Lucky Wheel.

Enter Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Strange Mirror in Scrooge's Store. Head up to the top left corner, where Oogie Boogie will be standing next to the broken Wheel, and give him the Genuinely Lucky Wheel.

Oogie Boogie then reveals the surprise he has for you this week: you must play his various mini-games and collect an Oogie Boogie Tile from each one. You need to collect a total of four Oogie Boogie Tiles to complete this Quest. Note that you can also ask Oogie Boogie for more information about any of his mini-games.

Head up to the Genuinely Lucky Wheel and spin it by approaching the lever on the left and selecting the Interact prompt when it appears.

You need to spin the Genuinely Lucky Wheel a total of five times to receive your Oogie Boogie Tile. You are guaranteed to get the Tile on your fifth spin. Spins one through four will reward you with a variety of items, such as:

On your fifth spin, a Red Chest containing the Tile will appear. Open the Chest and claim your reward!

Whack-a-Pumpkin, the mini-game that first appeared during the Quest A Halloween Invasion , is back again! To begin a game of Whack-a-Pumpkin, head to the fenced-off area in the center of the upper floor of Oogie Boogie's Lair. There is a stack of dice with a pumpkin-shaped button on it. Approach the button and press "Interact" to start a game.

While the game is active, pumpkins will pop up in a 3 x 3 grid inside the fence. Use your Royal Pickaxe to whack the pumpkins as they appear.

You must whack a total of 10 Pumpkins to earn an Oogie Boogie Tile. The Tile will appear at the entrance to the play area as soon as you have whacked your tenth Pumpkin. Each game is timed, with a pumpkin-shaped countdown timer appearing on the wall, but you can play as many times as you like until you earn your Tile!

Because the pumpkins show up so quickly, and it takes several steps for you to cross the grid, I recommend standing in a corner and focusing on 3-4 spots per game, rather than running around trying to hit every Pumpkin as it appears. Here is where I typically stand to maximize pumpkin whacking: In addition, unequip your Companions before playing so they don't get in your way!

Go fishing in the Lava Pond on the first floor of Oogie Boogie's Lair to catch an Oogie Boogie Tile. When the tile appears is random, so you may have to fish several times to catch it. A new set of bubbles will appear repeatedly, so you will not need to wait between casts.

There are five Oogie Boogie Smiles hidden around his Lair. They are glowing green, much like the fake furniture you had to locate during the Quest Rescue Mission .

To claim a Hidden Smile, simply approach it and select the "Remove" prompt when it appears. The five Hidden Smiles can be found in the following locations:

On the bottom dice of the two-dice stack just in front of where Oogie Boogie is standing.

On the face of the middle skeleton of the Oogie Boogie's Wall Skeletons decoration in the small fenced-in area to the left of where Oogie Boogie is standing.

On the grandfather clock against the back right wall of the Lair, behind the fenced-in area where you place the Oogie Boogie Tiles.

To the left of the Oogie Boogie Skeletons on the right wall of the Lair's upper level, just in front of the fenced-in area where the Tiles are placed.

On the interior of the fence around the Whack-a-Pumpkin game, just to the left of the entrance.

After you have removed all five Hidden Smiles, the Oogie Boogie Tile will appear in the fenced-in area with the wall skeletons, near where Oogie Boogie is standing.

After collecting all four Oogie Boogie Tiles, head to the Tile Mini-Game on the right side of Oogie Boogie's Lair's upper floor, to the right of the Whack-a-Pumpkin game. Approach the tile puzzle and select the Interact prompt when it appears, then place all four tiles you collected in the designated slots.

Use your Royal Shovel to complete the Tile Puzzle and create the correct image of Oogie Boogie's face. There are three different versions, and you need to figure out which is the correct one. Here are some hints to help you solve the puzzle:

Oogie Boogie doesn't like showing off the bugs inside him, because he sees them as a weakness.

The Boogieman wants to show himself as being bigger and stronger than his nemesis Jack Skellington.

Oogie Boogie wants you to create a scary version of his face, and he doesn't find bats particularly scary.

The completed tile puzzle looks like this:

As soon as you solve the Tile Puzzle, large green cracks begin appearing around the Mirror Lair. Return to the Lucky Wheel and talk to Oogie Boogie to ask him what is happening. However, he refuses to tell you, and simply tells you to get out.

Leave Oogie Boogie's Lair via the Mirror to complete the Quest. Although you won't see a specific popup indicating this, you get a Lucky Wheel furniture item as your reward!

articles.title: Giovanni Simeone y su pasión por el coleccionismo Pokémon: "Moví cielo y tierra para conseguir esa carta''
articles.standfirst: El futbolista ha hablado en un vídeo de YouTube del Torino sobre esta afición que comparte junto a sus hermanos
articles.summary: El futbolista ha hablado en un vídeo de YouTube del Torino sobre esta afición que comparte junto a sus hermanos
articles.body: El fútbol no es la única pasión de Giovanni Simeone. El delantero argentino del Torino es un auténtico aficionado al universo Pokémon y, especialmente, al coleccionismo de sus cartas. Una afición que le acompaña desde pequeño y que ha recuperado con fuerza en los últimos años, hasta el punto de convertirla también en un proyecto empresarial junto a sus dos hermanos. El vínculo de Gio con Pokémon viene de lejos. Durante su infancia ya coleccionaba cartas y disfrutaba de los videojuegos de la franquicia, aunque hubo una época en la que dejó aparcada esta afición. Sin embargo, un compañero de profesión terminó despertando de nuevo su interés por este mundo. Así lo explicó el propio futbolista en un vídeo publicado recientemente en el canal de YouTube del Torino, en el que mostró parte de su colección y compartió algunas de las historias que hay detrás de ella. El propio Simeone contó cómo volvió a interesarse por las cartas Pokémon durante su etapa en el Hellas Verona. Todo comenzó cuando su compañero Faraoni apareció con algunas cartas que había comprado y que había pedido que le enviaran al centro de entrenamiento. "De niño coleccionaba cartas, pero lo dejé. Luego hubo un día en el que un compañero, Faraoni, cuando estaba en Verona, había comprado unas cartas y había pedido que se las enviaran al centro de entrenamiento. Empezó a enseñarme algunas y me dijo que esas cartas valían mucho dinero. Entonces llamé a mi madre y le pregunté por mis cartas de pequeño. Me dijo que tenía una caja enorme de cartas antiguas de Pokémon. En ese momento le pedí que me las enviara", explicó. A partir de ahí, el argentino volvió a conectar con una afición que había marcado su infancia. De hecho, su colección no se limita únicamente a Pokémon, ya que durante el vídeo también reconoció que guarda cartas de otros juegos tan populares como Magic: The Gathering y Yu-Gi-Oh. Entre todas ellas, hay una que tiene un significado especial para él: el Pikachu inspirado en Vincent van Gogh. Se trata de una de las cartas más cotizadas y reconocibles de las ediciones especiales de Pokémon, y conseguirla no fue precisamente sencillo para el delantero. "Moví cielo y tierra, llamé a gente de todo el mundo para conseguir que me enviaran esa carta. Finalmente encontré una y la tengo en mi colección", relató Simeone al enseñar esta pieza tan especial. Pero la pasión de Giovanni por las cartas coleccionables va mucho más allá de reunir ejemplares para su colección personal. El futbolista comparte esta afición con sus dos hermanos y juntos han impulsado Game Brothers, un proyecto empresarial centrado en la compra, venta y distribución de cartas coleccionables. Pokémon y One Piece se encuentran entre las principales franquicias de su catálogo, aunque su actividad también abarca otros productos relacionados con este universo. La empresa ofrece álbumes, fundas protectoras, accesorios para conservar las cartas en buen estado y diferentes artículos de merchandising. De esta manera, Simeone ha conseguido unir dos mundos que, a priori, parecen muy alejados: el fútbol profesional y el coleccionismo de cartas. Una afición que comenzó durante su infancia, que recuperó casi por casualidad gracias a un compañero de equipo y que hoy comparte con sus hermanos a través de un proyecto empresarial.

articles.title: OpenAI Boss Sam Altman Addresses Backlash After Saying It Was 'Terrible' for People to Have RAM in Their PCs
articles.summary: OpenAI boss Sam Altman has addressed the backlash over comments he made in a recent interview, where he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center.
articles.body:
OpenAI boss Sam Altman has addressed the backlash over comments he made in a recent interview, where he said he thought it was “terrible” for people to have RAM in their PCs rather than a data center .

Speaking to YouTuber Cheeky Pint , Altman said: "From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer, and being used 5% of the time. Like, you want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."

The comments were widely ridiculed, with many suggesting that, whether he intended it or not, Altman sounded like he wanted to take away personal ownership of memory and force society to use resources for the benefit of AI companies such as his. Social media was flooded with posts, images, and videos of people slamming Altman for the suggestion, promising to protect their memory from any who might try to claim it. Even tech rival Elon Musk joined the backlash with a meme of his own .

The people deserve to have their RAM too! — Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 1, 2026

The people deserve to have their RAM too!

Now, in a series of posts on social media, Altman expressed frustration at the online response, insisted his comments had been taken out of context, and even joked about the situation, renaming his X / Twitter name to 'Ram Altman' at the suggestion of a follower.

Altman said he actually wants the world to have “tons of memory,” and for people “to put as much as they want in their computers.” He added that it was “f***ing annoying” that this was “taken out of context.”

“I have been arguing for the world to ramp up memory production for a long time,” he continued.

@HarshithLucky3 i lol'd — Ram Altman (@sama) November 4, 2026

Here, Altman isn’t denying that he believes RAM would be better served in data centers, rather that there is enough RAM to go around. "I want you to have so much RAM," Altman said in another reply . "Let's build more."

The response to Altman’s response was, predictably, further memes and dunks, with many, particularly within the PC gaming community, continuing to hit out at the tech billionaire’s views.

Altman had initially taken to X / Twitter to issue a statement that some are taking as a response to the Democrats’ decisive victory over Trump’s Republicans during yesterday’s U.S. midterm elections. The Democrats have now taken control of U.S. Congress, which perhaps signals a change in approach the regulation of AI, which up to this point has been pretty much nonexistent.

“People should always be in control of the future,” Altman tweeted . “OpenAI is against the notion that it would be acceptable for people to be relegated to a role of doing things that ‘AI systems think makes sense to reward in humans.’

“People should not cede control of the future to superintelligence, and that requirement should ultimately constrain AI progress.”

Data centers and the potential impact on jobs and humanity’s very existence from AI is a key issue for voters. Meanwhile, the AI boom has led to a scarcity of memory to power it, which in turn has caused graphics cards, video game consoles, and PC components to skyrocket in price. Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all raised the prices of their consoles as a result of the ‘RAMpocalypse,’ while the RTX 5080 just disappeared off of Nvidia's marketplace, weeks after the RTX 5090 was all but discontinued.

Photo by Alexi J. Rosenfeld/Getty Images.

Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

articles.title: The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel Teaser's In-Universe Quote Sparks Timeline Speculation
articles.summary: This week's tease for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel didn’t give us much to work with. Eight years since the last mention of the game, and all we got was a CGI sand dune. But that hasn’t stopped fans speculating about what it all means.
articles.body:
This week's tease for The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel didn’t give us much to work with. Eight years since the last mention of the game, and all we got was a CGI sand dune. But that hasn’t stopped fans speculating about what it all means.

Most of the speculation is centred around the quote that ends the teaser trailer. “The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil lifted thinly to my eyes,” it said. “A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.”

The quote was attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest of High Queen Irande of Hammerfell, where Sentinel is likely set. The year? 4E 206.

While this is clearly the year the quote was recorded, fans are wondering if that’s also when the game will be set. If so, it would mean Sentinel takes place just five years after the events of Skyrim, which in turn would mean the Dragonborn’s achievements would be fresh in the memory of people across Tamriel.

"Most of the issues present in Cyrodiil as of Skyrim (like the encroachment of the Aldmeri Dominion) likely still apply," redditor HowdyHangman77 suggested . "We’ll likely find out from some obscure book or one-off dialogue what happened with the Stormcloak Rebellion (given the Empire’s waning power across Cyrodiil, I suspect it succeeded, but who knows)."

“This quote being 4E 206 doesn't mean the game will take place around then, but it's possible,” said Inner-Chance . “If that is when it takes place, the Dragonborn will likely be in Skyrim during the events of Sentinel. We would probably see dragons coming over the border and the civil war would almost certainly not have a victor yet. What else would this mean for Sentinel if this is the timeline of the game?”

Dragons were one of the standout features of Skyrim — seeing them flying overhead, attacking villages and towns in unscripted ways. Those are some of the best emergent moments in TES history, so you can imagine Bethesda wanting to build upon those systems as well as riding on the popularity of Skyrim, the studio’s most-played game.

Hammerfell is a huge area that borders Skyrim, Cyrodil and High Rock. Dragons don’t care about borders. A five-year jump from Skyrim leaves the outcome of Skyrim's civil war and regional political tensions intentionally ambiguous. In the Fourth Era, Hammerfell transformed from a fractured Imperial province into an independent, sovereign nation.

The Thalmor, an Elven supremacist political faction and extremist paramilitary force of the Aldmeri Dominion, were promised a large chunk of Hammerfell by Emperor Titus Mede II in 4E 175 in an attempt to end The Great Warm which saw the elven armies launch a surprise attack on southern Hammerfell in 4E 171, overwhelming the Imperial Legions and forcing a retreat across the desert. The Redguards saw this peace offering as a betrayal and refused to hand over their lands. As a result, Hammerfell was renounced and became a sovereign nation.

By the time of the Dragon Crisis in Skyrim, Hammerfell exists as a battle-hardened republic. While a deep bitterness remains toward the Imperial throne for abandoning them, the indigenous Redguards maintain active trade and diplomatic ties with individual provinces like High Rock. Sentinel could see the Thalmor march north once more as dragons raid from the east. It’d make for an interesting geopolitical setup for an Elder Scrolls game.

Countering this speculation though is the suggestion that Sentinel could be set decades or even hundreds of years after Skyrim, and the quote we see in the teaser is nothing more than a snippet from a lore book detailing ancient history, or a prophecy only now coming to pass in the distant future.

"All we know is that the game is set AT LEAST 5 years after Skyrim, it very well could be 20, 50, or 100 years after," one fan said. "5 years after the events of Skyrim, a Moth Priest had a prediction about the future, glimpsed in an Elder Scroll. How far into the future, we just don't know," suggested another.

It's worth remembering that Skyrim takes place 200 years after Oblivion. Will Bethesda jump forward centuries, as it has done before, for Sentinel? Last month, The Verge reported that Sentinel will dive into the history of the Elder Scrolls themselves, allowing players to discover their secrets firsthand for the first time.

We've got plenty more on The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel in the wake of Bethesda's announcement, including word that it is reportedly still at least two years away from launch , and an in-depth explanation of what Sentinel means .

articles.title: Nexus Mods Forces Mandatory AI Disclosures and Filters, Explains Why It Won't Ban AI Mods
articles.summary: Nexus Mods has reacted to the deluge of AI mods by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.
articles.body:
Generative AI has taken over the modding scene, with modders mashing together existing games and using AI-assisted code to, for example, put the Nemesis system from Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor into Rockstar's Red Dead Redemption 2 .

Nexus Mods, the biggest platform for mods on the internet, has reacted by enforcing mandatory disclosure for mods with AI-assisted code, and letting users filter AI-assisted mods out of their search criteria or preferences.

"We are pro-human creativity," Nexus Mods co-owner Victor 'Foledinho' Folmann said in a blog post , before further explaining why the site won’t outright ban AI mods entirely.

“You may ask me why [we won’t ban AI mods], since that is not the solution some of you were looking for,” he said. “The answer is simple: AI is currently used throughout the whole process of creation, from script autocompletion to generation of textures, voices, and full assets, and it is difficult to draw a clear boundary between what is acceptable and unacceptable."

Foledinho believes an outright ban would just encourage modders to hide AI use. “It should be out in the open, clearly labelled, and regulated according to the rules that we can implement on our platform," he said.

Modders will have to declare whether their mod is AI-assisted, primarily AI-generated, or features promotional material generated by AI. A “public explanation of how and where AI was used” is also required on the mod’s page.

The use of AI in development is perhaps the hottest topic in the video game industry. While Steam has an AI discosure policy for store pages, Valve does not limit AI-focused developer access to its platform, nor block "AI slop" from from it despite complaints from fans and developers about the deluge of low effort games that flooded the recent Steam Next Fest . Valve also put the onus on developers to ensure their game stands out amid the detritus. In particular, there’s been a big issue on Steam of developers having their games instantly cloned with AI as soon as they share any development progress.

"Rather than relying on a single mechanic that someone can easily copy, you need to keep growing your game by adding features, personality, and creativity that stem from your own perspective," Valve’s Tom Giardino recently said.

Epic Games boss Tim Sweeney recently called mandatory AI disclaimers “a political act,” criticizing Steam and Valve in particular. Meanwhile, indie game storefront Itch.io recently deleted what it called “terabytes of AI slop” flooding its service. "Just because you can upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models doesn't mean you should upload 10 terabytes of poorly optimized AI generated models," Itch said.

As for Nexus Mods, existing mods have a 60 day grace period to comply with the new rules. If they haven’t updated by January 2, they potentially face account restrictions. "As I said before, this is a complicated subject, and I don't expect everyone to agree with every decision we've made, or will make in the future," Foledinho added. "We've had to consider many sides and preferences when discussing it all; some people would prefer to prohibit AI-generated content entirely, while others embrace it and want fewer restrictions. We've considered both sides, but ultimately we need to make decisions we believe are right for Nexus Mods and our community as a whole."

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time never gets old
articles.summary: Nintendo is releasing a full-on remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on November 5th that reimagines the N64 classic on the Switch 2.
articles.body: Breath of the Wild changed everything. Two decades after The Legend of Zelda made the transformational shift to 3D, Breath of the Wild reinvigorated the franchise with an open-ended adventure that was built around player freedom and expression. Instead of following a set path, players could go wherever they wanted and tackle challenges in a variety of ways. That philosophy filtered down to subsequent games, letting players author their own creative solutions to puzzles in titles like Tears of the Kingdom and Echoes of Wisdom. As a result, Zelda has never been bigger, and the traditional, more linear Zelda games had become a thing of the past. Or so it seemed. For one of the biggest Switch 2 exclusives so far, Nintendo has gone back to Ocarina of Time, which originally launched on the N64 in 1998. It’s one of the most influential and revered games in the long-running franchise, a game that showed that the classic Zelda formula — one that used a large world to connect a handful of intricate, puzzle-filled dungeons, creating a grand adventure — could work in three dimensions. Now Ocarina has been remade for the Switch 2 in a way that accomplishes exactly what a good remake is designed to do: preserve the core of the original experience while making it more accessible for modern audiences. And it shows there’s still some life left in the traditional Zelda formula. The story remains unchanged from the original. It’s a third-person action-adventure game where you play as a little forest dweller named Link who gets pulled into an adventure to save the fantasy realm of Hyrule from a villain named Ganondorf. That’s true of basically every Zelda title, and here the twist comes from a musical instrument (the titular flute-like ocarina) imbued with magical powers. Over the course of the game you learn songs that can change the weather, warp you across the landscape, mess with the flow of time, and more. [Image: The original Ocarina was renowned both for its large 3D world and for the intricacy of its dungeons, which required using the ocarina, along with various other items, to solve puzzles in clever ways. At a certain point you’re even jumping back and forth in time, navigating spaces as both tiny Link and his adult version. The challenge steadily grows in complexity right up until you face Ganondorf in his castle, forcing you to use a huge range of items at your disposal. The most notable difference in the remake is how it looks. Gone are the blocky, fuzzy N64-era graphics, which have been replaced with something that blurs the line between fantasy art and realism. While it’s not a fully open world like Breath of the Wild, this version of Hyrule, which has a large open field that connects a series of dungeons and villages, is still incredibly lifelike; everything from rushing water in a lake to the swaying grass outside of a ranch looks and moves in realistic ways. The flip side is that, while the characters are more detailed than before, they’ve been rendered with a style inspired by puppets and stage shows. It’s a tricky balancing act that the game mostly nails. The characters look like exaggerated caricatures, but at the same time they’re imbued with such a level of detail that they don’t feel out of place against the more realistic backdrops. Link is the best example; while his face almost looks like a porcelain figure, his outfit is like something a real adventurer would wear, made by weaving together grasses found in Kokiri Forest, where he lives. It looks great in practice — although Ocarina does suffer from some frustratingly dark areas, like in most modern games — and it also sets the remake apart from the rest of modern Zelda adventures. The Breath of the Wild line has a fantastical, Studio Ghibli-inspired look, while the top-down spinoffs have cutesy, toylike graphics. Ocarina splits the difference and comes out looking like something distinct, yet unmistakably Zelda. The Switch 2 graphics also do a great job of heightening the emotion. There’s an incredible sense of grandeur when you first walk into the stark Temple of Time, with a single ray of light illuminating the dark interior. Iconic moments like wandering blindly through the desert take on a new sense of tension and terror because of how the game looks as sand whips around you, obscuring your view of the harsh landscape. Fighting Dark Link on a foggy, desolate beach was enough to get my heart racing. [Image: Perhaps more important than the visual update is a number of smart gameplay changes. Early 3D games can be awkward to play now because designers were still working out how best to navigate 3D spaces. The Ocarina remake fixes this in a few ways. For one thing, you now have free camera control, making it possible to look anywhere by moving the right stick, just like in any modern game. This makes it easier to keep your eye on enemies around you or spot important details for solving a puzzle. The game now also lets you jump whenever you want — in the original Link could only jump at designated points — which makes moving around in spaces feel less restrictive. Other modern touches include being able to equip items quickly with the D-pad instead of having to go to the pause menu, and the “threads of time,” which is a fancy name for a tool that tracks your quests so you can more easily figure out what to do next. As an example of how much these tweaks can impact the experience, let’s revisit the infamous Water Temple. Over the years since Ocarina of Time first launched, this dungeon has become known primarily for being extremely difficult. It involves constantly playing a song to make the water rise and fall so you can access different levels, while also frequently equipping iron boots that cause Link to sink to the bottom when necessary. With the original controls this was tedious and frustrating. But I didn’t find it difficult at all in the remake; I could quickly equip the boots whenever I needed to, and the camera allowed me to clearly see what I needed to do. The Water Temple was always a well-designed dungeon hindered by the technology of the time. In the remake, I could fully appreciate what the developers were going for. There are a handful of other changes — expanded dialogue, the ability to hum songs into the Switch 2’s microphone, the fairy Navi thankfully toning down her annoying hints — and they all build toward the same goal: enhancing the original without changing its essence. Unlike a lot of classic games, the original Ocarina of Time is still relatively easy to play; it’s available through a Switch Online subscription, and the 3DS version from 2011 remains a great port. But the remake does enough to make it the ideal way to play, particularly for that big new audience of Zelda fans that started with Breath of the Wild. More importantly, it’s proof that Zelda can be many things simultaneously. And that’s an exciting prospect for Hyrule’s future. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launches on the Switch 2 on November 5th.

articles.title: How Long Is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Remake?
articles.summary: You may think you know how long The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, but things have changed in the remake. Here's how many hours you'll need to spend with your Switch 2 to finish it.
articles.body:
How long is The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time? You may well think you know the answer if you’re one of the many millions who hold Link’s first 3D adventure close to their hearts. But the remake is here almost 30 years later, and things have changed a little.

So, just how much time should you put aside to finish the Switch 2 Ocarina of Time remake, and can you squeeze it in before GTA 6 arrives? We have three different accounts for you to read through, which detail just how many hours it took, and how that time was spent.

60 The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time Switch 2 Screenshots

Logan Plant — Senior Editor, Playlist & DB, IGN

I’ve spent 45 hours with Ocarina of Time on Switch 2, across two separate save files. Before I get into my time spent, I will point out that Ocarina of Time only supports one save file ! It kind of gives the impression that it supports multiple – when you start a new game, it only warns you that the five autosave points will be overwritten – but manually saving on your new file will overwrite your original file. I almost lost my 100% file this way, but luckily grabbed it from the cloud save.

Onto my stats: It took me 21 hours to reach the credits, and nine more (for a total of 30 hours) to 100% Ocarina of Time. That’s every Piece of Heart, Gold Skulltula, Empty Bottle, and so on. I probably could have done it faster than this; I estimate I took five-ish hours just living in the world and absorbing all of its fine details. Pre-existing knowledge of the original is definitely an enormous help. You can rip through some puzzles, quests, and boss fights when you know exactly what to do.

Then, I did it again. I started a new game and beat it in roughly 14 hours. This was mostly mainlining it – and it went fast given that I had literally done all of it just days before – but I still took some extra time to smell the roses and do some extra quests. Up next is the three heart challenge: I’ve never tried that before, but Ocarina’s lack of a hero mode makes me want to set my own challenge. For all my thoughts on those 45 hours, you can check out my Ocarina of Time review .

If you take out the time I spent hunting for differences compared to the original game and riding Epona about Hyrule Field, it took me about 27 hours to fully complete Ocarina of Time. That's finishing the story and doing every side quest, alongside finding all of the Heart Pieces and Gold Skulltulas. (And spending at least half an hour doing the Horseback Archery minigame because I've always been rubbish at it.) I will openly admit to being a massive Ocarina fan, so I know this game like the back of my hand, which definitely helped in getting through it as quickly as I did.

One aspect I loved about the Switch 2 remake was picking out all of the subtle changes the developers have made to the dungeons. Especially the Water Temple, for obvious reasons. Playing a Zelda game over Christmas is a tradition of mine, so I'm looking forward to a second playthrough where I'll relax and enjoy the world more. And by that I mean spend far too much time riding Epona around Lake Hylia.

Brendan Graeber — Senior Editor, Guides, IGN

As our resident Zelda guides expert who has been helping readers through dungeons since A Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds, I tend to take my time when going through Hyrule, making sure I’ve documented every last Piece of Heart, Gold Skulltula, and suspicious-looking rock. In searching every inch of Hyrule Field for anything not found in the original game (did you know fairies leave notes now?), my playtime tends to be a bit extended, leaving me at around 27 hours when I achieved 100% completion and beat the game. Granted, even with some of the new changes, it’s fair to say I grew up on these streets, so more often than not I knew exactly where to go and look for secrets. Still, I haven’t spent as much time as I’d like in the Hall of Fallen Foes, and I’m looking forward to replaying some of my favorite boss battles!

articles.title: The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time Review, Gameplay Impressions, Videos & Top Features for Switch 2
articles.summary: The top-rated video game of all time is now better than ever.
articles.body:
The top-rated video game of all time is now better than ever.

Widely regarded as the one of the most influential games ever, a crown jewel of Nintendo's library and the pinnacle of The Legend of Zelda series, Nintendo has outdone themselves remaking The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time to provide fans with the definitive way to experience this masterpiece.

Whether it's your first time or tenth time, this is a must-play for any gamer.

In 1998, Ocarina of Time was influential for its finely-tuned action combat featuring Z-targeting lock-on gameplay, camera control, item management, level design, puzzles, expansive world and time-traveling mechanics. It's easy to see its influence across the industry since its release. Nintendo has perfected the classic in every way while while staying true to the core aspects and charm of the original instead of straying away from what made it a success nearly 30 years ago.

Ocarina of Time features smooth combat with precise, responsive controls. Fans of the original version will feel an instant improvement while fans of recent Zelda games like Breath of the Wild and Tears of the Kingdom will feel right at home with the modern control scheme. Thanks to the advanced hardware of the Switch 2 and its Joy-Cons and Pro Controller, gyro aiming makes a major difference when aiming arrows, enhancing long-range combat and improving archery mini-games to be far more enjoyable. It's easy to take this for granted in 2026 since other Nintendo games have implemented this feature but it is an important feature that makes this version superior to the original.

In addition to improved combat, the modernized control scheme makes exploration and puzzles feel less of a chore. For example, players can equip/unequip important items with one press of the D-pad instead of needing to go into a menu. The frustration many experienced with the Water Temple on Nintendo 64, for example, is gone. Pressing the R button quickly pulls up all available items, making for quick and smooth adjustments during gameplay. Easily switching from the bow to bombs or hookshot makes a major difference allowing players to effortlessly engage in combat and puzzles without breaking flow.

In addition to modernizing menus and item mapping, players can roll into a dash by holding down the A button and there's also now a dedicated jump button instead of Link jumping automatically in the N64 version. Although these may seem like minor adjustments given today's standards, they make a significant difference in making Ocarina of Time even more enjoyable to play.

The biggest and most notable difference of course will be the overhauled presentation and graphics. The storybook-like presentation, movie-quality art style, incredible graphics, shadow work, physics and textures are the best from Nintendo. The immense attention to precise detail to all environments and interiors, in addition to the cutscenes direction and amazing camera work create an epic feeling fit for such an important game in history. The cinematics are truly jaw-dropping and unbelievable, some of which capture the true terror of villainous Ganondorf and other cutscenes that really sell the devastation across Hyrule.

Beyond graphics, audio design is phenomenal across the board. The sound effects and epic presentation of discovering an upgrade remains a classic staple that is nearly unmatched in gaming. The music, voice acting and sound effects are top notch, allowing gamers to really feel the emotion through the music. The implementation of music is very impressive. For example, intense music begins when enemies engage, which is a great feature to let the player know an enemy is near in case they didn't see but also makes gameplay even more exciting. A nice quality-of-life feature is conversation log that allows players to revisit dialogue in case they missed something or need to check.

The world building, distinct environments and varied locations have always been one of the most memorable aspects of Ocarina of Time. It is a true joy being able to explore Hyrule to discover secrets, uncover alternate paths, interact with different characters, solve puzzles and unlock upgrades. There are interconnected quests, which are easy to follow thanks to modern quality-of-life features for tracking quests and objectives. There's an excellent map system, similar to recent Resident Evil games, with clearly defined points of interest, including entrances/exits, heart pieces and chests.

Fantastic level design and puzzles, which will make players think about their surroundings and equipment but solutions aren't obtuse for the sake of being obtuse like many other games or even some other games in the Zelda series. Ocarina of Time is the quintessential Zelda game and deserving of the high praise it has received since 1998. It is the pinnacle of the series for a reason and it's primarily because navigating through the world is enjoyable and doesn't feel like a chore or demanding players waste their time with overly-confusing puzzles or design choices. Players can immersive themselves in the atmospheric nature of each distinct location. The unique temples have enjoyable gimmicks to keep the game fresh and maintain a fantastic pace.

In addition to exploring temples during the main quest to save Hyrule from Ganondorf, Link can partake in min-games such as archery, bombchu bowling and one of the enjoyable fishing mini-games in all of gaming. These mini-games are enjoyable ways to improve a player's combat skills but also serve as important ways to unlock upgrades so they are absolutely worth the player's time.

A game as revered as Ocarina of Time required the utmost care and attention to detail as possible. The quality in every aspect is top notch and the game runs smoothly on Switch 2 without any crashes or glitches.

Overall, limitations and drawbacks from the Nintendo 64 and Nintendo 3DS versions are eliminated in this remake thanks to the advanced hardware of the Switch 2. There are excellent quality-of-life features such as ideal autosave points, modernized camera control and impeccable performance. This is arguably the finest-crafted and highly-produced title in Nintendo's library and befitting to honor a legendary classic as beloved as Ocarina of Time. A dream remake for gamers for years, Nintendo absolutely delivered in every way possible to perfect this masterpiece in gaming history.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is held in such high regard because it is a grand adventure that players often don't want to end. It is a game so enjoyable many will want to immediately begin again. Now in 2026 on Switch 2, gamers have the definitive way to experience this classic masterpiece.

For those who have never played Ocarina of Time, it absolutely lives up to the hype and it exceeds expectations on Switch 2. This is sure to have people clamoring for Majora's Mask and many more remakes of classic games in the series. Whether released in 1998 or now perfectly remade in 2026, it is easily a contender for Game of the Year.
